entities.summary: Kenneth Paul Scharf is an American painter known for his participation in New York City's interdisciplinary East Village art scene during the 1980s, alongside Jean-Michel Basquiat and Keith Haring. Scharf's do-it-yourself practice spanned painting, sculpture, fashion, video, performance art, and street art. Growing up in post-World War II Southern California, Scharf was fascinated by television and the futuristic promise of modern design. His works often include pop culture icons, such as the Flintstones and the Jetsons, or caricatures of middle-class Americans in an apocalyptic science fiction setting.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent figure in New York City's East Village art scene alongside Jean-Michel Basquiat and Keith Haring, Kenny Scharf contributed to the city's vibrant cultural landscape of the 1980s. His DIY practice influenced the development of street art and performance art during this period.
